name: Gregor's Remains
summary: Coleman Farthing seeks Gregor's Remains to settle an old score. The bones belonged to Gregor Agamand, once a member of Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest family.

sections.title: A Legacy of Ruin
sections.body: Before the Third War, the Agamands held great wealth and broad lands across northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge invaded Lordaeron, the family patriarchs chose pride over flight. They fortified their mills and urged their loyal laborers to stand against the undead. The defense failed. The estate fell, and those who stood their ground were butchered and raised into undeath. Gregor Agamand became a mindless servant of the Lich King, haunting the mills his family had ruled.

sections.title: The Price of Vengeance
sections.body: Some who escaped the Lich King's control joined the Forsaken, but the memory of that defense still wounds them. Coleman Farthing, a former mill worker now stationed in Brill, blames the Agamands' pride for trapping his soul in eternal rot. Farthing seeks Gregor's remains as personal retribution against the master who led his household into damnation.

faq.answer: Gregor Agamand was a prominent member of the Agamand dynasty, Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest land-owning family before the Third War. When the Plague of Undeath arrived, he and his family fortified their estate instead of fleeing. The Scourge slaughtered and raised everyone inside.

faq.q: Why does Coleman Farthing want Gregor's Remains?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing once worked at the Agamands' mills. He resents the family for persuading their workers to stay and fight the Scourge, a choice that condemned them all to undeath. He seeks Gregor's remains as long-delayed vengeance.
Gregor Agamand's risen form at the Agamand Mills in the northern hills of Tirisfal Glades yields the remains.

faq.q: Are the Agamands part of the Forsaken?
faq.answer: No. Gregor Agamand and his kin remain mindless servants bound to the Scourge, unlike the Forsaken who broke free under Queen Sylvanas.

angles.text: The Agamand tragedy echoes the fate of many Forsaken: ordinary folk betrayed by noble pride and abandoned to the horrors of the Plague.
Clearing the Agamand Mills strikes at Scourge forces still threatening Tirisfal Glades.
